source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.habit: Much-branched perennial herb, erect to ascending stems 40–60(–120) cm tall
morphology_source_reported.pubescence: Stems, blade undersides and inflorescences strigose with noticeable white hairs
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Usually trifoliolate, rarely 5 leaflets basally; leaflets 10–50 mm long, up to 6(–12) mm wide, narrow elliptic to oblong; conspicuously gland-dotted on both surfaces
morphology_source_reported.inflorescence: Many crowded flowers in erect to drooping racemes
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Corollas usually 5–7 mm long; calyces heavily gland-dotted
morphology_source_reported.fruits: 7–9 mm long, densely gland-dotted, not cross-wrinkled and exserted from the calyx

habitat_source_reported: Sandy or rocky prairies, open woods, roadsides
cautions: Historical Psoralidium tenuiflorum synonym crosswalk confirmed by Kew POWO and USDA GRIN; morphology remains Flora-sourced and pending independent QA.
Regional occurrence is not evidence of local BONAP nativity
